status: PROVISIONAL — integrity fixes to a checker that is not proved sound (XVII.B5, G1-G3 open)

fixes.name: time-of-check/time-of-use on the object file
fixes.defect: scan_object(path) verified the digest, then replay_frontier() reopened the path with NodeReader::open(path, offset). A file changed between the two opens would be replayed while the reported derivation digest described different bytes.
fixes.fix: scan_object now reads the file once into an immutable Vec<u8>, verifies the digest over that buffer, and parses the header, tables and node records from it. ObjectScan owns the buffer; both replay modes read node records from scan.bytes (node_reader/next_node) and payloads are borrowed slices. The path is never reopened.
fixes.test_evidence: TOCTOU BOUND: replay used the scanned bytes, not the replaced path
fixes.test_detail: Scans object A, copies a different valid object B over A's path, then replays from the scan: it validates A with A's derivation digest, while validate_with on the now-B path is refused.

fixes.name: node budget enforced only after the scan
fixes.defect: The node budget was checked inside the replay loop, after the scan had already sized per-node arrays from the object's declared node count. A hostile object could request a large allocation before any limit applied.
fixes.fix: scan_object(path, budget) now receives the budget. It refuses with BudgetExceeded when the declared node count exceeds the budget, and does so before allocating the consumer array. Every other declared count (hypotheses, axioms, imports, registry, types, type arguments, terms) is bounded by the bytes actually remaining in the verified body before Vec::with_capacity, and every payload length is a bounds-checked slice (Cursor::take).
fixes.test_evidence: BUDGET BEFORE PARSE: refused: replay reached node 1000, over its budget of 10
fixes.test_detail: A 1000-node chain object is refused by scan_object with budget 10 (reached = 1000, the declared count) and scans at budget 1000.

fixes.name: alpha_eq resolved shadowed binders outermost-first (found while replaying the bignum object)
fixes.defect: alpha_eq's ordav walked its binder environment front-to-back, i.e. outermost-first, while HOL Light's ordav walks its list head-first (innermost-first). With a shadowed binder (`\q. ... \q. ...`) it reported alpha-inequality for an alpha-equal pair, so term_remove kept a hypothesis HOL Light had removed. The retained hypothesis contained a free variable, and a later ABS was refused: the real arm/add object failed at node 363 with `ABS: variable free in hypotheses` in both frontier and retained modes, and with the pre-IX.85 checker too.
fixes.fix: ordav now iterates the binder environment in reverse (innermost binding first), matching HOL Light.
fixes.test_evidence: test tools::proof_object::tests::alpha_eq_follows_innermost_shadowing ... ok; and the real arm/add object, which was refused at node 363 before, now VALIDATED.
fixes.test_detail: Compares `\q. (\q. q) q` with `\x. (\q. q) x` (alpha-equal, shadowed) and `\x. (\q. q) y` (not alpha-equal).

tests.workspace: all test binaries ok (cargo test --offline); doc-tests 3 passed
